_doc: Course registry — the one place a course is listed. tools/study/build-registry.js turns it into the STUDY array in site-chrome.js (menu, next-course chain) and the cards + JSON-LD in study.html. Order within a lane is the order here. Art history: dates shown on the timeline; technique: "course · N parts" is counted from the data.

card.text: how to recognize the greek and roman myths in art, from an athenian wine cup to titian, rubens, ingres and turner.
how to recognize a japanese woodblock print, from moronobu and harunobu to utamaro, sharaku, hokusai, hiroshige and yoshitoshi.
how to recognize rococo, from watteau, boucher and fragonard to tiepolo, carriera and the wieskirche.
how to recognize neoclassicism, from hamilton, west and mengs to david, canova and girodet.
how to recognize romantic painting, from fuseli, blake and goya to friedrich, géricault, delacroix, constable, turner and the american landscape painters.
how to recognize realist painting, from daumier, courbet, millet and manet to menzel, repin, homer and eakins.
how to recognize impressionism, from manet and monet to morisot, degas and cassatt.
how japanese prints changed western art, from whistler, manet, monet and degas to van gogh, cassatt, lautrec, bonnard and dow.
how to recognize post-impressionism, from seurat and cézanne to van gogh, gauguin, toulouse-lautrec and rousseau.
how to recognize fauvism and early expressionism, from matisse and derain to kirchner, kandinsky, marc and schiele.
how color works for painters, from light and the color wheel to contrast, mixing and mood, shown with historic color plates and public-domain paintings.
how light and dark build form, from the value scale and the order of light and shadow to kinds of light, edges, chiaroscuro and tenebrism.
a short course on how painters arrange a picture, from the frame and value massing to balance, movement and unity, with plates from two classic public-domain books and public-domain example works.
what paintings are made of, from pigments and binders to panels, canvas and grounds, and how colors change with time.
a short course on how oil and acrylic paint differ, from how each dries to how each ages, with historic plates, original diagrams and example paintings.
